title: WCM Adds a World Model to the Critic for VLA Reinforcement Learning
summary: Posted on July 31, 2026 by Tongji University, Shanghai Innovation Institute and Fudan University, the World Critic Model attacks a structural flaw in reinforcement-learning post-training of vision-language-action policies: critics that score value from a single frame are mismatched with the partial observability of real robot control, and naively feeding in observation history is both expensive and insufficient, because scalar-return regression alone never teaches cross-temporal dynamics. WCM builds the critic on a lightweight LeJEPA architecture that jointly predicts future latent state and estimates value, so the representation is explicitly trained on temporal structure. It drops into both on-policy and off-policy pipelines and works with Pi0, Pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT backbones. Across 149 tasks in four benchmarks it sets state of the art in and out of distribution, with the largest gains on generalization, and it holds up on seven real-world manipulation tasks under off-policy RL.
whyItMatters: RL post-training is how VLAs get past what imitation can teach, and the critic is the part everyone reuses from single-image value estimation without asking whether it fits a partially observed robot. Diagnosing that as a state-approximation problem — and fixing it with a world-modelling objective inside the critic rather than a bigger critic — is a cleaner answer than adding history frames. Because it slots into existing pipelines behind Pi0, Pi0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT unchanged, it is the kind of result that propagates into other people's training runs quickly.
